title: Illinois's 16th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Illinois's 16th Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Representative Darin LaHood against Democratic nominee Paul Nolley. LaHood, first elected in a 2015 special election and currently serving on the House Ways and Means Committee and the House Intelligence Committee, is seeking another term in a district that spans 21 counties across central and northwestern Illinois. Nolley, the executive director of Project First Rate and a first-time candidate, is challenging LaHood on a platform of prioritizing working families, ending corporate PAC influence, and preserving Social Security and Medicare. The district has been held by a Republican for 98 of the last 100 years and is considered safely Republican by major election forecasters.
polling_note: No publicly available general election opinion polls were found for this race as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Darin LaHood
candidates.summary: Darin LaHood is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Illinois's 16th Congressional District, first elected in a September 2015 special election. He serves on the House Ways and Means Committee (Chairman of the Subcommittee on Work and Welfare) and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and previously served in the Illinois State Senate from 2011 to 2015 and as an Assistant U.S. Attorney in Nevada and an Assistant State's Attorney in Illinois. LaHood is the son of former U.S. Secretary of Transportation and former U.S. Representative Ray LaHood.

candidates.name: Paul Nolley
candidates.summary: Paul Nolley is the Democratic nominee for Illinois's 16th Congressional District in the 2026 election. A lifelong resident of the Rockford area, he is the executive director of Project First Rate, a nonprofit that helps young people access apprenticeship programs and skilled trades careers. Nolley previously worked with faith-based and community organizations including the YMCA, United Way, and Habitat for Humanity, and is a first-time candidate for public office.

forecast.rationale: No general-election polling exists for this race as of June 2026, so the forecast rests entirely on non-polling structural indicators — which is why confidence is medium rather than high. Those indicators are remarkably consistent: Darin LaHood is a long-serving incumbent (since 2015) on the powerful Ways and Means and Intelligence Committees; the district has voted Republican in 98 of the last 100 years; major nonpartisan forecasters rate the seat safely Republican; and Democratic challenger Paul Nolley is a first-time candidate with no elected office experience. The combination of a strong incumbent, deeply Republican district history, and a novice challenger points to an overwhelming Republican advantage consistent with a safe_r rating and an estimated win probability well above 95%.
